subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
Vijay,
I told you on the bus that I was going to tell someone, and I did. I'm writing so you hear it from me, not from anyone else.
You said your uncle gets angry at night and that you've started sleeping in your school clothes in case you need to leave. You made me promise not to say anything. I can't keep that one. It's not the kind of secret a friend should carry alone.
After last period I went to the counsellor, Mrs Lhamo. She listened to all of it, said none of this is your fault, and before I had even left her room she had called the school's safeguarding lead. She's coming to find you before home time today.
You can be angry with me. I would still rather you be angry and safe.
Pema

qa.q: What had Vijay started doing at night?
qa.a: Vijay had started sleeping in school clothes in case of needing to leave.

qa.q: How does Pema feel about breaking the promise, and what shows it?
qa.a: Pema feels the weight of it but is sure it is right, writing, "I would still rather you be angry and safe."

qa.q: Which steps made Pema's choice wise?
qa.a: Pema told Vijay first on the bus, went to the counsellor that same day, and wrote so Vijay would hear it directly, instead of keeping a secret about danger.

qa.q: How might Vijay feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Vijay may feel angry and exposed at first, but also cared for, since Pema acted to keep Vijay safe and gave warning first.

grounding: A teenager knows a friend's secret about danger at home is not theirs to keep, tells the friend first, and brings it to the counsellor, who acts the same day.

subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
The hardest thing I did in Class 9? Okay. I'm Wasim. My friend Vinita had been chatting with someone online who said he was seventeen. He kept telling her, "Don't tell your parents about us, they won't get it," and then he asked her to meet him alone on Sunday.
She showed me the chat, all excited, and made me swear. I felt sick. I said, "Vinita, I can't keep this one. I'm telling my mum today, and you can come with me."
She was furious. But she came. Mum read the chats, stayed really calm, told Vinita none of it was her fault, and called Vinita's mother right then. That evening they blocked and reported the account together. Vinita didn't talk to me for a week. Then she said thanks.

qa.q: What did the online contact ask Vinita to do?
qa.a: He asked her to meet him alone on Sunday.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling when Vinita showed the chat?
qa.a: Wasim felt sick with worry, because the demand for secrecy and the request to meet alone were warning signs.

qa.q: What made Wasim's response a safe one?
qa.a: Wasim refused to keep the secret, told Vinita first, and went to Mum the same day; she called Vinita's mother and they blocked and reported the account.

qa.q: How did Vinita's feelings change over the week?
qa.a: She was furious at first and felt betrayed, but after a week she thanked Wasim, perhaps seeing the danger more clearly.

grounding: A teenager recognises that an online contact's demand for secrecy and a solo meeting is danger, tells the friend first, and brings in a trusted adult that day.

subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
I sit behind Varun and Binita in maths, so I saw most of it, though I can't say what either of them was thinking.
On Wednesday, Binita showed Varun something on her phone and giggled. I heard her whisper, "He's nineteen. He wants to meet me alone on Saturday. Don't tell anyone, promise." Varun didn't laugh. He went very still.
At lunch, he found her by the water cooler. I heard him say, "I'm not keeping this one. I'm going to tell Ma'am, today. I'd rather you be angry with me than something happen to you."
Binita said, "You're such a baby," and walked off.
In the last period, Varun went to the counsellor's room. Ten minutes later, the counsellor came and quietly asked Binita to come with her. I heard later that her mother came to school that same afternoon.
Binita didn't speak to Varun for a week. Then, one morning, she left a chocolate on his desk.

qa.q: How old was the person who wanted to meet Binita?
qa.a: He's nineteen.

qa.q: What does Varun going very still suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests Varun felt alarmed and worried for Binita, sensing the meeting was dangerous even though she was giggling.

qa.q: Which choice showed real care, and why?
qa.a: Varun told Binita first that he would tell, then went to the counsellor the same day, putting her safety above keeping her secret.

qa.q: How might Binita have seen Varun at first, and later?
qa.a: At first she was angry and called him a baby, but leaving a chocolate on his desk suggests she later felt grateful.

grounding: A classmate observes a teenager refusing to keep a dangerous secret, telling the friend first, and going to a trusted adult the same day.

subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
Thursday. After tuition, Karthik told Leela his plan: on Saturday night he would take his father's motorbike, without a licence, to race some older boys on the highway. "Don't tell anyone. Swear."
Leela's stomach dropped. "Karthik, I'm not keeping this. It's dangerous. I'm going to tell my mother tonight."
"You're such a traitor."
That evening, Leela told her mother everything. Her mother listened, thanked her, and called Karthik's mother straight away. Leela heard her say quietly, "I think you need to know this tonight."
Friday. Karthik didn't sit with her at lunch. He told the others she was a snitch. Leela ate alone, angry and hurt, and wondered if she had ruined everything.
The following Tuesday, Karthik caught up with her on the stairs. "One of those boys crashed on Saturday. He's in hospital." He looked at the floor. "My dad took the keys. I'm… glad you told."

qa.q: What did Karthik plan to do on Saturday night?
qa.a: He planned to take his father's motorbike, without a licence, to race some older boys on the highway.

qa.q: How did Leela feel eating alone on Friday?
qa.a: Leela felt angry and hurt, and doubted herself, wondering if telling had ruined the friendship.

qa.q: What did Leela and her mother do that kept Karthik safe?
qa.a: Leela told Karthik she would tell and then told her mother that evening, and her mother called Karthik's mother straight away.

qa.q: How does Karthik see Leela's choice by the next Tuesday?
qa.a: After hearing about the crash, Karthik feels grateful and a little ashamed, admitting he is glad she told.

grounding: It shows a teen who refuses to keep a friend's dangerous secret, tells him first and informs a trusted adult the same evening.

subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
Mehak, you asked what to do if a friend tells you something frightening and says "don't tell." Let me, your Abhinav Mama, tell you about my hostel days.
I was sixteen. One night my roommate sat on my bed and said he didn't want to be alive anymore. He made me promise to tell no one.
I was scared. I thought, if I tell, he'll hate me. But I also knew this was not a secret I could hold. So I said, "I care about you too much to keep this. I'm going to wake the warden now, and I'll stay with you."
We went together. The warden sat with him all night, called his parents that same night, and the next day a counsellor came.
He was furious with me for a month. Then, years later, at my wedding, he hugged me and said, "You were right." Sometimes, Mehak, caring means breaking the silence.

qa.q: Who did young Abhinav wake that night?
qa.a: He woke the warden.

qa.q: How did young Abhinav feel when his roommate made him promise?
qa.a: He felt scared and torn, afraid his roommate would hate him, but sure this secret could not be kept.

qa.q: What choice in the story kept the roommate safe?
qa.a: Abhinav told the roommate he couldn't keep it, stayed with him, and woke the warden that same night; the warden sat with him and called his parents.

qa.q: How did the roommate feel about Abhinav over time?
qa.a: At first he was furious for a month, but years later he felt grateful and said Abhinav was right.

grounding: An uncle recalls refusing to keep a roommate's self-harm-risk secret, telling him first and involving the warden the same night.

subtype: When a secret must be told [Response]
passage:
On the school trip to Mahabaleshwar, the dorm lights went out at ten, and Tanvir whispered across the bunk. "Promise you won't tell? There's this guy online. He's twenty-four. He says I'm mature. He wants to meet when we're back, and says not to tell my parents. He's asked for photos."
Tejas's stomach went cold. "Tanvir, that's not okay. Someone who asks you to hide things from your parents isn't safe."
"You promised."
"I didn't. And this one I can't keep. I'm telling you first: I'm going to Mr Pillai. Tonight."
Rain drummed on the tin roof, and there was no signal. Tejas walked down the dark corridor and knocked until Mr Pillai opened the door.
Mr Pillai listened, then sat with both boys. "You did the right thing, Tejas. Tanvir, this is not your fault. Let's block him right now. We'll call your parents first thing when there's signal, and report the account together."

qa.q: What did the man online tell Tanvir not to do?
qa.a: Not to tell his parents.

qa.q: How did Tejas feel when Tanvir described the messages?
qa.a: Tejas's stomach went cold; Tejas felt alarmed and protective, knowing a man who asks for secrecy from parents isn't safe.

qa.q: What did Tejas do that makes this the right kind of secret-breaking?
qa.a: Tejas told Tanvir first that this secret couldn't be kept, then went that night to Mr Pillai, who blocked the contact and planned to call the parents and report.

qa.q: How might Tanvir feel after Mr Pillai says it's not his fault?
qa.a: Tanvir might feel embarrassed and upset with Tejas at first, but also relieved and safer, knowing adults are handling it.

grounding: Shows a teenager knowing a friend's secret about a dangerous online contact is not his to keep, telling the friend first and then a teacher that night.
